task_snapshot.title: Add a skip_blank option to indent
task_snapshot.description: indent prefixes every line, including blank ones; add a keyword-only skip_blank flag that leaves empty and whitespace-only lines untouched.
task_snapshot.problem_statement:
Add a `skip_blank` option to `textkit.indent.indent`.

Today `indent(text, prefix)` prefixes every line, including blank ones:

    >>> from textkit.indent import indent
    >>> indent("a\n\nb", "> ")
    '> a\n> \n> b'

Add a keyword-only parameter `skip_blank: bool = False`:

- With `skip_blank=True`, a line that is empty or contains only whitespace is returned unchanged: no prefix, and its own whitespace is kept. All other lines are prefixed as before.
- Line endings, including `\r\n`, are preserved exactly, and no newline is added or removed.
- The default (`skip_blank=False`) behaves exactly as today, and existing calls of the form `indent(text, prefix)` keep working.

Example: `indent("def f():\n\n    pass\n", "    ", skip_blank=True)` returns `"    def f():\n\n        pass\n"`.

`tests/test_indent.py` must keep passing.
acceptance_criteria: skip_blank is a keyword-only parameter defaulting to False
With skip_blank=True, empty and whitespace-only lines are left unchanged
hints: A line from splitlines(keepends=True) still carries its line ending; ignore it when deciding whether the line is blank.
